Alright, let me sit down and think about this year's plan. I've been farming these 16 mu for two decades now, so I pretty much know what works and what doesn't.

---

**My situation this year**

Me and my wife do most of the work on the farm. Our son works in Handan in a factory — he comes back to help during wheat harvest and maize planting when things get tight, but we can't count on him for the daily work. Our daughter is still in school. So it's really two and a half pairs of hands most of the year.

I've got 16.1 mu total. I keep it split like I have for the past few years: about **6 mu in the west field for cotton**, and **10.1 mu running the wheat-maize rotation** like most families in the village. The cotton field drains better and the soil there is a bit sandier — not as good for wheat anyway. The other block is flatter and holds water better, suits the wheat-maize cycle.

I know some of my neighbors have given up on cotton — too much labor at picking time, and the price goes up and down. But I still keep a few mu because when cotton has a good year it brings in real cash, and the wheat-maize rotation barely covers the household expenses after inputs. My older neighbor Lao Zhang quit cotton last year and moved everything to wheat-maize; I'll watch how he does before I decide to follow him.

---

**Winter wheat (already in the ground — 10.1 mu)**

I planted the wheat back in mid-October, like I do every year. Used the same variety as last year — bought from the agri-supply shop in town, a local improved type, about 15 yuan per mu worth of seed. I put down about 15 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before planting along with some urea mixed in as a base — that gives me roughly 10 kg N at base.

Now in spring, I need to topdress. The extension guy a couple years back told me wheat needs most of its nitrogen at jointing. I usually put another 10 kg of urea per mu around then, which works out to about 5 more kg N. So total N will be around 15-17 kg per mu. I don't go higher — urea is 2400 yuan a ton these days and I've seen that pushing above 20 kg N just makes the wheat lodge when there's a heavy rain.

Irrigation: I'll run the well maybe 3 times — once in spring before greening-up if it's dry, once at jointing when I topdress, and once at grain filling. Each irrigation costs me around 30 yuan per mu in pumping, so I'm careful. Last year we had a dry April and I did 4 times — the yield was decent, about 430 kg/mu, but my electricity bill was ugly.

I'll spray a herbicide once in spring (broadleaf weeds come up fast), and I usually buy a little fungicide mix for scab at heading — scab ruined a field two years ago and I don't want to take that chance again. Harvest will be around June 7-12 depending on the heat.

Expected yield: around 420 kg/mu. That's what I got last year and the year before, roughly.

---

**Summer maize (follows wheat — 10.1 mu)**

The tight part of the year. Wheat comes off around June 10, and I need to get maize in within a week or the yield drops. I'll hire the combine for wheat harvest (about 50 yuan/mu), and the same driver usually has a no-till maize planter he rents out (another 20 yuan/mu). No time to plow — I just plant straight into the wheat stubble. That also saves me fuel.

Seed is hybrid — I buy fresh every year, no sense saving maize seed. About 30 yuan per mu. I'll go with the variety my cousin planted last year; he got over 500 kg/mu with it on similar soil.

Fertilizer: I put down a compound as base right at planting, about 30 kg of 18-15-10 per mu. Then when the maize is knee-high in late July I topdress urea — about 20 kg/mu. So total N around 14-15 kg/mu. Maize wants nitrogen but it can't afford too much either.

Irrigation: if July rains are normal, I might only need to irrigate once at tasseling. If it's dry I'll go twice. Usually 1-2 times.

Pesticide: mainly a herbicide right after planting for weeds. Corn borer used to be bad but since the neighbors all started using resistant hybrids it's less of a problem. I'll spray insecticide if I see a real infestation but not preventively — too expensive.

Expected yield: 470 kg/mu. Harvest end of September.

---

**Cotton (6 mu, single crop)**

Cotton is where the real work and money is. I plant mid-to-late April — usually around the 20th if the ground temperature looks right. I use Bt hybrid seed (kangchong mian), costs about 30 yuan per mu. Without Bt the bollworm would eat me alive.

I plow the cotton field in early April, put down base fertilizer — compound 15-15-15, about 40 kg per mu. Then I'll topdress urea once at squaring (early July), another 15 kg/mu. Total N comes out around 13 kg/mu, plus the P and K from the compound. Cotton doesn't need as much N as people think — too much N means too many leaves and not enough bolls.

Irrigation: I'll water twice — once after planting to get the seedlings up if it's dry, once at flowering. The cotton field is further from my well so pumping is a bit more expensive.

Pesticide: This is where cotton gets expensive. Even with Bt I need to spray for aphids, lygus bugs, spider mites. I'll spray maybe 4-5 times over the season. I also use a herbicide at planting and a growth regulator (mepiquat) to keep the plants from getting too tall. About 50 yuan/mu in chemicals.

Picking is the hard part. My wife and I will pick the first round in mid-September, and I'll need to hire help for the second and third pickings in October. Maybe 8-10 days of hired labor at 80 yuan per day. The daughter helps on weekends.

Expected lint yield: 260 kg/mu. Last year I got 250, year before 270 — depends on the weather in August mostly.

---

**What I'm watching**

Prices. If cotton stays low into summer I might cut back next year. Also the well — the water table keeps dropping, neighbors are saying the village may put limits on pumping. If that happens, I'd have to rethink everything, maybe move more area to wheat-maize since maize in the summer uses the rainy season.

Cash is tight. I'm hoping to keep total inputs under about 7500 yuan this year. Any subsidy that comes through the village for wheat or seed helps.
